title: Acceleration at an Instant Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A bus pulls away, a ball rolls to a halt, a lift starts to rise. In all three, velocity is changing. Outside Diya's college an ambulance sets off from the gate and its speed climbs every second. But how fast is the speed itself climbing, at one exact instant? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 2, Motion in a Straight Line) we learn average and instantaneous acceleration.

On a live motion notebook the ambulance starts from rest with v = 4t - t²/4. We shrink the time gap from 4 s to 0.01 s and watch the averages close in on 3 m/s² while the chord on the v-t graph turns into the tangent. Then we derive a = lim Δv/Δt = dv/dt step by step, see why speed goes up when v and a point the same way and down when they point opposite ways, and learn what a negative sign really means, with two pause-and-think questions. A worked example, the exam trap about zero velocity at the top of a throw, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Three cases, one idea: the ambulance at the gate
0:25 What is acceleration? Unit m/s²
0:44 Live sim: an ambulance from rest
1:14 Shrink the gap: the averages close in on 3 m/s²
1:48 The rule: a = dv/dt, step by step
2:32 Same or opposite direction + pause and think
3:04 What a negative sign really means
3:40 Worked example: v = 3t² + 2t
4:17 Exam trap: zero velocity, zero acceleration?
4:42 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:22 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Uniform and Non-Uniform Motion. Same change every second, or not?
